title: Adaptive prefetch load harness for KV prefix cache — p95/regression alerting
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a repeatable, CI-friendly harness to evaluate KV/prefix cache policies under realistic mixed workloads and to detect regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency. This ticket scopes the adaptive prefetch variant (prefetch window + admission control) and integrates its metrics into our regression detector so we can automatically block or flag runtime changes that worsen p95 or memory cost for a given hit rate. The deliverables are: 1) a parametrized load generator (kv-runner) that can run on CI agents and on perf clusters; 2) a set of synthetic workloads that mimic our production prefix distributions; 3) dashboards and alerting rules for p95, tokens/sec, and cache memory; 4) a regression detection job that compares new runs vs baseline and annotates PRs.
acceptance_criteria: kv-runner can run on Github Actions / perf-cluster and produce stable metrics (tokens/sec, p95, hit_rate, cache_memory) as Prometheus-style CSV
A canonical synthetic workload (3 mixes: conversational short-turns, long-context generation, and embedding-heavy prefixes) with seedable generators is in repo runtime/perf/kv-harness
Regression detector evaluates new run vs baseline and fails CI if p95 increases by >10% with hit_rate >= baseline and cache_memory increases by >15% for equal hit_rate
Dashboards (Grafana) for per-shard p95, median tokens/sec, hit-rate heatmap, and memory-usage vs hit-rate curve are published and linked in the ticket
Proof-of-concept run comparing current admission policy vs adaptive prefetch shows measurable trade-offs documented in 'runs_summary'
test_plan: Parameters: cache_size (MB), prefetch_window (tokens), admission_threshold (frequency), eviction_policy (LRU/size-aware), workload_mix (A/B/C)
Run grid over cache_size: [256, 512, 1024] MB; prefetch_window: [0, 32, 128] tokens; admission_threshold: [1, 4, 16] occurrences; 3 repeats per cell
Load profile: 60s warmup, 10m steady-state (burst profile modeled from production trace), 60s cool-down; measure per-second tokens and latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99)
Measurement hooks: extract per-shard p95, tokens/sec, cache hit-rate, resident memory RSS, and eviction counts at 1s granularity
Failure criteria: flakiness measured as >10% variance across repeats for p95 or tokens/sec triggers re-run and investigation

Regression detection: compare new run median p95 vs baseline median p95 for the matching workload_mix and cache_size; if p95 delta > +10% AND hit_rate >= baseline_hit_rate - 2%, fail CI; annotate PR with CSV artifact and link to Grafana snapshot
runs_summary: Baseline (current admission policy) on perf-cluster-3: workload_mix=A (conversational short-turns), cache_size=512MB, prefetch=0 -> tokens/sec=12.8k, p95=82ms, hit_rate=72%, cache_rss=470MB
Adaptive prefetch (prefetch=32, admission_threshold=4) same cell -> tokens/sec=13.9k (+8.6%), p95=95ms (+16%), hit_rate=78% (+6%), cache_rss=540MB (+14%)
Adaptive prefetch increases throughput and hit-rate but worsens p95 beyond our 10% threshold for this config; demonstrates trade-off and need for shard-level p95 caps or selective prefetch gating
Long-context mix (workload_mix=B) shows smaller p95 impact and larger tokens/sec gains — suggests workload-dependent policy recommended
artifacts: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 — kv-runner: add adaptive-prefetch flags and prometheus CSV output
